note: Sample work descriptions and expert scores were written by the build team so the flow can be shown. A real practitioner must replace each expert_score before any teacher is verified for real. Never show expert_score to a teacher.

scale.2: Needs rework before it can be used
scale.3: Good: does the job, small points to improve
scale.4: Very good: could be shown as an example

items.work: A learner stitched a salwar kameez side seam. The seam is straight and even, the thread tension is good, and the raw edge is finished with an overlock.
A learner stitched a blouse sleeve. The seam puckers along its length and the stitch length changes from long to short in several places.
A learner sewed a hem on a school uniform. The hem is even, but there are two skipped stitches and the thread ends are not tied off.
A learner says the machine skips stitches and answers by tightening the top thread tension fully. They did not check the needle or the threading.
A learner took measurements for a kurta: chest, waist, shoulder and length. All are written down, but the chest was measured over a thick jacket.
A learner kept a daily cash book for a grocery shop for a week. Every sale and purchase has a date and an amount, and the closing balance matches the cash in the drawer.
A learner wrote a tax invoice but left out the buyer's name and the invoice number. The tax is calculated correctly.
A learner entered a purchase on credit as a cash payment, so the shop's cash balance shows less money than it really has.
A learner prepared a monthly sales summary in a spreadsheet. The totals are correct, but the columns have no headings.
A learner explained that a small shop below the turnover limit may still need to register if it sells goods to another state. They said to check the rule on the official portal.

name.hi: स्थानीय दुकानों के लिए डिजिटल मार्केटिंग

items.work: A learner made a post for a sweet shop: a sharp photo of the sweets in daylight, a short line in Marathi, the shop's phone number and the address.
A learner made a post for a tailor with a blurry photo taken in the dark. The text is long, has spelling mistakes and has no contact details.
A learner set up a shop's business profile with the right opening hours and a map pin, but the photos are old and the phone number is missing.
A learner replied politely to a customer's question about price on the shop's page, in the customer's language, within the hour.
A learner promised the shop owner that 1,000 new customers will come in a month.
A learner wired a training board: switched the main switch off and put a tag on it, tested that the circuit was dead, used the right colour wires and fitted the earth to the socket.
A learner joined two wires with plain twisting and no tape or connector, then left the joint outside a junction box.
A learner wired a socket correctly but used red for neutral and black for live. They also did not label the circuit.
A learner changed a bulb holder after switching off at the wall switch only, without turning off the main switch.
A learner laid conduit in neat straight runs with saddles at even spacing, and all bends are smooth and wires are not strained.
A learner opened a motor only after switching off and removing the fuse, laid the parts on a clean cloth in order, and photographed the wiring before disconnecting it.
A learner pressed a new bearing onto a shaft by hammering on the outer ring, and the bearing is now noisy and tilted.
A learner refitted a motor and checked that the shaft turns freely by hand, but did not check the terminal tightness.
A learner tested a repaired pump by switching it on with the guard removed and the shaft coupling uncovered.
A learner replaced a worn pump seal, cleaned the seat and refitted it with the right sealing surface. There is a small drip when first started.
A learner changed a cracked screen: powered the phone off, took out the battery connector first, kept the screws in order and tested the touch before sealing.
A learner opened a phone without disconnecting the battery and used a metal tool close to the board.
A learner told a customer that the data on the phone would be safe, then wiped it to fix a software problem without asking.
A learner replaced a charging port and soldered it neatly, but there are two small solder bridges that they did not notice.
A learner wrote down the phone's faults and the price before starting, and the customer agreed. They also kept the old parts in a labelled bag.
A learner helped a villager apply for a certificate on the official portal. They filled the form together, read each answer back, and gave the customer the receipt number.
A learner asked a customer for the bank PIN and the OTP on their phone so that the learner could finish the transaction faster.
A learner typed a customer's form correctly but did not save a copy of the scanned documents and left them on the shared computer desktop.
A learner explained to an older customer, in the customer's language, how to check their account balance, and made clear that the bank never asks for the PIN on a call.
A learner kept a daily register of every service, the fee taken and a receipt number, but the fee column sometimes has no entry.
A learner photographed a family at a wedding in daylight. The faces are sharp and well lit, the background is not cluttered, and several poses are taken in case someone blinked.
A learner filmed a function by holding the phone upright and moving it fast from side to side. The video is shaky and the sound is mostly wind noise.
A learner edited a two-minute shop advertisement. The cuts are clean and the text is readable, but the music is louder than the voice and drowns it out in places.
A learner took a product photo of a handloom saree against a clean cloth with the light coming from a window. The colours look true and the weave pattern is visible.
A learner put a customer's family photos and videos on social media for the shop's advertisement without asking the family first.
